title: Choosing a site for a new port
body: A coastal country plans to build a new port for its growing trade with Europe. Two sites are being studied. Site A lies on a straight stretch of coast that faces the open ocean, where strong winds and high waves are common for much of the year. Site X lies inside a broad bay, where a curve of the coastline partly encloses the sea. The planners remember that the Bay of Bengal, the world's largest bay, has long been important for trade, and that the Persian Gulf has carried trade between India and Europe for thousands of years. After comparing the two sites, the planners recommend Site X for the new port and its dockyards.

title: A forest and a growing town
body: A town on the edge of a large tropical rainforest is growing quickly. Many families want more land for farms and houses, and some council members suggest clearing a large part of the forest. Others point out that the forest stores carbon, gives shelter to many rare animals and birds, feeds the rivers that the town depends on, and is home to indigenous villages whose people have protected it for generations. Scientists warn that cutting it down could lead to biodiversity loss and change the local climate, and that a cleared forest takes a very long time to recover. The council must decide what to do with the forest.
